title: pvVisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDReader
body:
## pvVisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDReader

Reads netCDF history files of the CCSM (Community Climate System Model) that hold one time record each; a list of files forms the time series. Use pvVisItNetCDFCCSM_MTSDReader when one file holds many records. The native pvNetCDFReader reads CF-compliant climate files and is usually the first choice. FileName takes a list of files, each one time step of a series (ParaView's file-series wrapper).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Opening a multi-record file with this variant shows only one time.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from CCSM netCDF data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The CCSM netCDF plugin offers the climate fields of the history file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MaterialStatus` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The CCSM netCDF plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MeshStatus` | Names of the CCSM netCDF meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The CCSM plugin reports the grid meshes of the file; take the names from the reader's available list. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from CCSM netCDF data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The CCSM netCDF plugin offers the climate fields of the history file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
